title: Challenge: tmux sessions that survive
intro: The tmux superpower: start work in a session, detach, even disconnect, your programs keep running. Reconnect later and pick up exactly where you left off. Let's do that loop. (Commands are checked, not executed.)

steps.instruction: Start a new tmux session named 'work'.
steps.success: [you're now inside tmux session 'work', a green status bar appears at the bottom]
steps.fail: Create a new named session. Use -s to name it.

steps.instruction: Detach from the session so it keeps running in the background. What do you press? (type it)
steps.success: [detached (from session work)], your shell is back, but 'work' keeps running.
steps.fail: Detach with the prefix key, then d. (Type 'C-b d' or 'detach'.)
steps.hint: Press Ctrl-b then d   (here, just type: C-b d)

steps.instruction: List the tmux sessions to confirm 'work' is still alive.

steps.success: [re-attached to 'work', everything exactly as you left it]
steps.fail: Attach back to the session named work.

done: Solved! new → detach → ls → attach. This is why people run long jobs and remote work inside tmux: a dropped SSH connection can't kill your session.
